doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Eddie Condon and being house clarinetist at his club
summary: Gordon knew Condon as a friend of his father, worked with him shortly before his death, and was house clarinetist at Condon's club for three years from 1978.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Tell me a little bit about your experience with Eddie Condon.

Well I didn’t know him very well but he was a very close friend of my father’s Eddie was. And I knew Eddie later on in life, just before he passed away. And I just started to work with him just before his death. I was working maybe a year or two before. I was working with him in New York City and I even asked him, I said, “Eddie I have a job, would you like to come out and play” and I called him up and he said sure he would. And we were all on cloud nine because Eddie Condon’s going to come out and play with us. But I didn’t know him that well but I appeared with him a couple of times, many times, but I didn’t know him that well.
And didn’t you go on to play in Condon’s?
Eddie Condon’s — I did Eddie Condon’s club in 1978, I was the house clarinet player there for three years.
Now what does it mean, perhaps we’ll have some people watching this that may not know what it means to be a “house clarinetist.”

Well a house clarinet player is the regular clarinet player that’s there every night, in and out, no matter who’s there you have to be there six nights a week, and you play from nine ‘til two in the morning or eight-thirty to one-thirty or whatever it is. But I was there for three years. The house clarinet player means just what it is, you’re the clarinet player for the club and you’re hired to do that. And that’s quite a long time to be in one place, for three years, at Eddie Condon’s. That’s quite a long time.
